info.name: LedgerOne - Accounting (Fiscal Period)
info.description:
Accounting module (Fiscal Period) API collection (Create, Get, List, Update, SoftClose, Close, Reopen). Reflects the implementation exactly as shipped in apps/api/src/shared/accounting. Does not modify or duplicate FinancialYear.postman_collection.json — this collection creates its own Financial Year fixture as a setup step, since every Fiscal Period must belong to exactly one Financial Year (00_BUSINESS_RULES.md Ch.6.1).

Design note (JWT required): same convention as FinancialYear.postman_collection.json — every protected request carries `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`, a long-lived (10-year) RS256 token pre-signed with the repo's own already-committed dev-only JWT keypair (.env's JWT_PRIVATE_KEY) for tenantId 900001.

Design note (no X-Tenant-Id validation-failure case): identical reasoning to FinancialYear.postman_collection.json — current-tenant.middleware.ts derives `req.tenantId` from the verified JWT claim and overwrites `X-Tenant-Id` in place, so this collection's `X-Tenant-Id: {{tenantId}}` header is inert structural consistency, not a real validation path.

Design note (repeatable overlap testing, isolated from FinancialYear.postman_collection.json's own fixture data): a collection-level pre-request script computes {{fpYear}}/{{fpYearEnd}} once per Newman invocation from a distinct offset/modulus (base 3000, not FinancialYear's own base 2030) so two separate runs of *this* collection never collide with each other's leftover rows, and this collection's own Financial Year fixture never collides with FinancialYear.postman_collection.json's separately-seeded rows under the same companyUuid — both write into the same `financial_years` table, so a shared date-range formula would risk cross-collection overlap failures.

Design note (one parent Financial Year, two Fiscal Periods): unlike FinancialYear's own collection (which needs two Financial Years to isolate lifecycle-transition testing on the Financial Year entity itself), this collection creates ONE Financial Year and TWO Fiscal Periods within it — the primary Fiscal Period (April) and a second, independent Fiscal Period (June) used both as the non-overlapping fixture for overlap-rejection tests and as an isolated entity for invalid-transition testing, without disturbing the primary Fiscal Period's own lifecycle sequence.

`validateFiscalPeriodOpen` is not exercised here — it is an internal Business-layer guard with no HTTP endpoint (mirrors `validateFinancialYearOpen`), not part of this module's public API surface. There is also no `open` endpoint — 00_BUSINESS_RULES.md Ch.6.5's lifecycle diagram documents no transition into Open other than initial creation (confirmed across the Repository/Business/Presentation milestones).

Known gap: List is unpaginated (07_REST_API_STANDARDS.md Ch.14 otherwise mandates cursor pagination) — same flagged Repository-layer limitation as Financial Year's/User Management's/Authorization's own list endpoints, not fixed by this collection.

Run order for a full pass, top to bottom: 'Create Financial Year (Setup) - Success' must run first to seed {{financialYearUuid}}; every Fiscal Period request chains off {{fiscalPeriodUuid}}/{{secondFiscalPeriodUuid}} set by 'Create Fiscal Period - Success'/'Create Second Fiscal Period - Success'.
